audit_findings.title: Raft creates a cash-and-earnings perimeter mismatch
audit_findings.magnitude: $450 million purchase price versus $270 million cash, a computed $180 million funding gap if all June cash were used
audit_findings.mechanism: Closing would remove cash from the equity bridge, add revolver interest to equity-level OE, and add Raft earnings, integration costs and reinvestment requirements.
audit_findings.evidence: We may also pursue acquisitions or other strategic priorities that will require additional liquidity beyond the liquidity we generate through our operations.
audit_findings.explanation: This is not a demonstrated error in the as-filed valuation because Raft had not closed and its assets, debt and earnings were not in the June financial statements. It is a forward-looking perimeter change that will make the current bridge obsolete upon closing. The net value direction cannot be determined because acquired earnings may offset cash consumption, financing costs and integration requirements.
audit_findings.action: At closing, use the post-acquisition balance sheet, final cash and debt funding, debt terms, purchase accounting, Raft historical financials, integration costs and sustainable maintenance investment to rerun OE, the bridge and every scenario.

audit_findings.title: A potentially nonrecurring license benefit remains in the anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Any nonrepeatable after-tax license profit inflates 2025 OE, the log-trend anchor and potentially the inferred growth rate.
audit_findings.evidence: This contributed to a gross margin increase of 100 bps attributed to a quantum cascade laser license for specific use in the quantum space, positive program performance on our Columbia Class program and favorable revenue mix as we realized increased revenue from our tactical radars.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that the license benefited 2025 revenue and margin, but it does not isolate the license contribution from Columbia Class performance and favorable mix within the reported 100-basis-point gross-margin increase. The $278.7 million anchor is only $10.5 million below 2025 OE of $289.2 million, so an unknown license contribution could pass substantially into the anchor, but the record cannot establish its materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the license revenue, associated costs, cash taxes and contractual recurrence terms; remove the nonrecurring after-tax contribution from 2025 OE, recompute the five-year trend and anchor, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: All cash is treated as surplus despite heavy operating liquidity needs
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $270 million, or $0.99 per diluted share and 6.5% of the $4,185 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Required operating cash should be excluded from the cash added in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Our working capital requirements and cash flows have historically been, and are expected to continue to be, subject to significant fluctuations.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates volatile working-capital needs, including $31 million of operating cash use in the first half of 2026, but it does not quantify a minimum reserve. Even the conservative extreme of treating all $270 million as operating cash reduces base value from $15.37 to approximately $14.38 per share and remains far below the $36.60 market price. It therefore cannot change the present overvaluation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Estimate minimum operating cash from quarterly working-capital troughs, contract funding cycles and revolver usage, then rerun the bridge with only demonstrably excess cash if a precise intrinsic-value or buy-below figure is required.

audit_findings.title: Tax-allocation agreement exposes DRS to an affiliate’s tax claims
audit_findings.mechanism: An affiliate tax liability collectible from DRS could require a bridge deduction or increase future cash taxes deducted in OE.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, to the extent US Holding fails to pay taxes imposed with respect to any consolidated, combined or unitary tax return of US Holding or any of its subsidiaries that includes us or any of our subsidiaries, the relevant taxing authority could seek to collect such taxes (including taxes for which US Holding or any of its subsidiaries is responsible under the tax allocation agreement) from us or our subsidiaries.
audit_findings.explanation: The agreement and joint-liability mechanism are demonstrated, but the record identifies no unpaid affiliate assessment, probable claim or collectible amount. The latest $50 million unrecognized-tax-benefit liability concerns recorded tax uncertainties and cannot be assumed to measure this separate affiliate exposure. Materiality therefore remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the tax-allocation schedules, open consolidated and combined return years, audit correspondence, affiliate payment history, indemnification terms and collectability analysis; deduct or incorporate into OE only exposure not already accrued.

audit_findings.title: Maintenance capital could be understated during capacity expansion
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; 2025 capital expenditures were $139 million versus $71 million of depreciation, a filed $68 million gap equal to 24.4% of the $278.7 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Additional maintenance capital reduces annual OE; if the spending supports forecast growth, omitting it also makes the growth cases internally inconsistent.
audit_findings.evidence: We will continue to make substantial capital expenditures and incur significant R&D costs aimed at improving our manufacturing capability, reducing costs, and developing and introducing new products and enhancements.
audit_findings.explanation: No maintenance-capex error is demonstrated because the filing identifies significant capacity expansion and does not classify the $68 million capex-over-depreciation gap between maintenance and growth. Nevertheless, the available gap is large relative to anchor OE and is reasonably capable of materially changing the valuation if a substantial portion is recurring or backlog-required.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile project-level capital spending, lease-financed facilities, replacement cycles and backlog-required capacity for each OE year; recompute OE and the trend using defensible maintenance-capex cases and rerun growth scenarios with the reinvestment required to support them.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded retirement obligations are omitted from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $17 million defined-benefit funded deficit at December 31, 2025; the June 2026 balance sheet carried $31 million of total pension and other postretirement liabilities
audit_findings.mechanism: Any retirement liability not already reflected through future OE should be deducted as a senior claim in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: We have unfunded obligations under our pension, postretirement and supplemental retirement plans, see Note 13: Pension and Other Postretirement Benefits to the Consolidated Financial Statements.
audit_findings.explanation: The omitted claim is demonstrated, but its scale is small. Even deducting the full $31 million June liability would reduce base value by only approximately $0.11 per share, from $15.37 to about $15.26, or 0.7% of base equity value, leaving the valuation conclusion unchanged. A full deduction may also overstate the correction because pension expense is already included in OE and the company expected $6 million of 2026 pension contributions.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile funded status, supplemental and postretirement liabilities, expected contributions and pension expense embedded in OE; deduct only the portion not already economically captured if refining the bridge.
